key_insight: Attention 'sink' tokens that are stable anchors in autoregressive LLMs are highly unstable across the denoising trajectory of diffusion language models (DLMs); pruning must account for this sink dynamics to be effective.
problem_solved: Reduces inefficient or harmful pruning in DLMs caused by reusing autoregressive sink-preservation heuristics that assume static attention sinks.
method: Measure attention-sink location and importance variance across the full diffusion/denoising trajectory to quantify instability in DLMs.
Derive a sink-aware pruning criterion that aggregates token/channel importance over timesteps (or adapts masks to sink dynamics) rather than preserving static sink positions.
Apply this pruning strategy to prune weights/heads/neurons while validating that generation quality and inference efficiency are preserved.
impact: Enables more reliable and effective compression of diffusion language models, lowering iterative denoising inference cost without relying on brittle AR-derived heuristics—useful for deploying DLMs in resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: AR model showing a single stable attention sink vs DLM showing shifting sinks over timesteps.
Line chart of attention-sink position/importance variance across timesteps for AR vs DLM.
Before/after scatter or bar chart comparing compute (latency/FLOPs) and generation quality (e.g., BLEU/perplexity) under standard vs sink-aware pruning.
Pipeline schematic: measure sink dynamics → compute sink-aware importance → apply pruning masks → validate generation.
paper_title: Sink-Aware Pruning for Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Aidar Myrzakhan, Tianyi Li, Bowei Guo, Shengkun Tang, Zhiqiang Shen
